domanda: Contoso plans to pilot self-service password reset (SSPR) before a tenant-wide rollout. Only the members of a Microsoft Entra security group named Pilot-Users must be able to reset their own passwords. All other users must continue to call the help desk. You sign in to the Microsoft Entra admin center as an Authentication Policy Administrator and browse to Entra ID > Password reset > Properties. What should you configure?
opzione_a: Set Self service password reset enabled to All, then create a Conditional Access policy that blocks the password reset flow for everyone except Pilot-Users.
opzione_b: Set Self service password reset enabled to Selected, then choose the Pilot-Users group.
opzione_c: Set Self service password reset enabled to None, then assign Microsoft Entra ID P1 licenses only to the members of Pilot-Users.
opzione_d: Set Self service password reset enabled to All, then set Number of methods required to reset to 2.
spiegazione: Correct: Microsoft Entra ID lets you enable SSPR for None, Selected, or All users. Selected scopes SSPR to the members of a chosen Microsoft Entra group, which is exactly the pilot requirement. A is wrong: the SSPR scope is controlled on the Password reset > Properties page, not by Conditional Access; Conditional Access does not gate the SSPR portal in this way, and setting the scope to All would already enable SSPR for everyone. C is wrong: None disables SSPR for all users, and licensing does not define the SSPR scope - the documentation explicitly states that although some unlicensed users may technically be able to access SSPR, licensing is not the scoping mechanism. D is wrong: Number of methods required to reset controls how many authentication methods a user must provide (the value can be set only to 1 or 2); it does not restrict which users are enabled for SSPR, and All would enable every user. Note also that Number of methods required to reset is configured on the Authentication methods page, not on the Properties page named in the scenario.
tags: sspr,self-service password reset,microsoft entra id,password reset scope,selected group

domanda: In the external collaboration settings of your Microsoft Entra tenant, Guest invite settings is set to "Only users assigned to specific admin roles can invite guest users". A project coordinator named Alena must be able to invite external partners for B2B collaboration. Alena must not be able to manage user accounts or any other directory objects. Which role should you assign to Alena?
spiegazione: Correct: The Guest Inviter role gives individual users the ability to invite guests without assigning them a higher-privilege administrator role. Users with the Guest Inviter role can invite guests even when "Only users assigned to specific admin roles can invite guest users" is selected. B is wrong: User Administrator is the other role that permits inviting guests under that setting, but it additionally grants broad rights to create, delete and manage user accounts and reset passwords, so it violates the least-privilege requirement. C is wrong: External Identity Provider Administrator manages identity provider configuration and external collaboration settings; it is not the least-privileged role for merely sending invitations, and it is not one of the two roles that the "specific admin roles" option refers to. D is wrong: Global Administrator is the most privileged role in the tenant and Microsoft explicitly recommends limiting it to emergency scenarios.
tags: b2b collaboration,guest inviter,external collaboration settings,guest invite settings,least privilege

domanda: Your Microsoft Entra tenant uses the email one-time passcode feature for B2B collaboration guests who cannot be authenticated by any other identity provider. A guest reports that the passcode she received stopped working before she could use it, and a different guest reports being asked for a new passcode the following morning. Which statement correctly describes the built-in lifetimes of email one-time passcode authentication?
opzione_a: One-time passcodes are valid for 30 minutes, and guest user sessions expire after 24 hours.
opzione_b: One-time passcodes are valid for 5 minutes, and guest user sessions expire after 90 days.
opzione_c: One-time passcodes are valid for 60 minutes, and guest user sessions expire after 14 days.
opzione_d: One-time passcodes are valid for 30 days, and guest user sessions never expire until the guest account is deleted.
spiegazione: Correct: Microsoft Learn states that one-time passcodes are valid for 30 minutes, after which that specific passcode is no longer valid and the user must request a new one, and that user sessions expire after 24 hours, at which point the guest receives a new passcode when they access the resource. B, C and D are wrong: they use plausible-looking but incorrect lifetimes. The 90-day and 14-day values are commonly confused with sign-in and refresh-token lifetimes elsewhere in Microsoft Entra ID, and no email one-time passcode session is unlimited - session expiration is deliberate added security for cases where a guest leaves their company or no longer needs access. Neither lifetime is configurable by the tenant administrator.
tags: email one-time passcode,b2b collaboration,guest authentication,otp,external id

domanda: A new Microsoft Entra tenant was created for Litware, Inc. No administrator has modified the external collaboration settings since the tenant was created. A security reviewer asks you what B2B collaboration guest users are currently able to see in the directory. Which Guest user access level is in effect?
opzione_a: Guest users have the same access as members (most inclusive)
opzione_b: Guest users have limited access to properties and memberships of directory objects
opzione_c: Guest user access is restricted to properties and memberships of their own directory objects (most restrictive)
opzione_d: Guest users have no access to any directory data until an administrator assigns them a directory role
spiegazione: Correct: "Guest users have limited access to properties and memberships of directory objects" is flagged as (Default) in the Guest user access list in Microsoft Learn. It blocks guests from certain directory tasks such as enumerating users, groups, or other directory resources, while still allowing guests to see the membership of all non-hidden groups. A is wrong: this option gives guests the same access to Microsoft Entra resources and directory data as member users, and it is not the default - it must be selected explicitly. C is wrong: this is the most restrictive option, under which guests can access only their own profiles; it is also not the default and must be selected explicitly. D is wrong: no such option exists; guests always receive a default set of permissions when they are added to the directory, and a directory role assignment is not a prerequisite for any directory read access.
tags: guest permissions,external collaboration settings,guest user access,default permissions,b2b

domanda: Six months ago you enabled self-service password reset (SSPR) by setting Self service password reset enabled to Selected and choosing a group named SSPR-Sales. The pilot succeeded, and the business now wants the members of a second group named SSPR-Finance to be enabled for SSPR as well. No other users may be enabled for SSPR. You must minimize administrative effort. What should you do from the Microsoft Entra admin center?
opzione_a: On the Password reset > Properties page, select both SSPR-Sales and SSPR-Finance under Selected.
opzione_b: Create a new group, add SSPR-Sales and SSPR-Finance as members of it, and select the new group under Selected.
opzione_c: On the Password reset > Properties page, set Self service password reset enabled to All.
opzione_d: Create a second password reset policy that is scoped to SSPR-Finance.
spiegazione: Correct: Microsoft Learn states that you can currently enable only one Microsoft Entra group for SSPR using the Microsoft Entra admin center, and that Microsoft Entra ID supports nested groups as part of a wider SSPR deployment. Creating a parent group that contains both existing groups as members and selecting that single parent group satisfies the requirement with the least effort. A is wrong: the admin center allows only one group to be selected for SSPR, so you cannot pick two groups. C is wrong: All would enable SSPR for every user in the tenant, which violates the requirement that no other users be enabled. D is wrong: Microsoft Entra ID has a single tenant-level SSPR policy for users - you cannot create multiple SSPR policies scoped to different groups (the separate, unchangeable administrator two-gate policy is the only other policy, and it is not something you create).
tags: sspr,nested groups,password reset scope,microsoft entra id,selected group

domanda: Fabrikam, Inc. synchronizes an on-premises Active Directory Domain Services forest to Microsoft Entra ID by using Microsoft Entra Connect. Every user is licensed for Microsoft 365 Business Standard only. You must allow the synchronized users to reset a forgotten password from https://aka.ms/sspr and have the new password written back to the on-premises directory. You need to identify the minimum licensing change required. What should you do?
opzione_a: Assign Microsoft 365 Business Basic licenses to the synchronized users.
opzione_b: Assign Microsoft Entra ID P1 licenses to the synchronized users.
opzione_c: Make no licensing change; Microsoft 365 Business Standard already includes self-service password reset with on-premises writeback.
opzione_d: Make no licensing change; enable password hash synchronization in Microsoft Entra Connect instead.
spiegazione: Correct: The SSPR licensing table on Microsoft Learn marks "Hybrid user password change or reset with on-prem writeback" as available only in Microsoft 365 Business Premium and Microsoft Entra ID P1 or P2. Of the choices offered, Microsoft Entra ID P1 is the minimum that enables writeback. A is wrong: the documentation explicitly warns that standalone Microsoft 365 Basic and Standard licensing plans do not support SSPR with on-premises writeback, so moving to Business Basic makes the situation worse (Basic does not even cover cloud-only password reset in the same way Standard does). C is wrong: Microsoft 365 Business Standard covers cloud-only user password change and cloud-only user password reset, but not on-premises writeback. D is wrong: password hash synchronization determines how sign-in is authenticated and synchronizes hashes from on-premises to the cloud - it does not write cloud password changes back to Active Directory, and it does not grant any license entitlement.
tags: sspr,password writeback,licensing,microsoft entra id p1,hybrid identity

domanda: The Microsoft Entra tenant for Contoso, Ltd. has the custom domain contoso.com verified, and Microsoft Entra Connect synchronizes identities from an on-premises directory. On the Password reset blade, Self service password reset enabled is set to All, Number of methods required to reset is set to 1, and the methods available to users are Mobile phone and Security questions. A cloud-only account that is assigned the Helpdesk Administrator role has registered security questions only, and cannot complete a reset at https://aka.ms/sspr. All non-administrator users can reset their passwords successfully. What is the most likely cause?
opzione_a: Cloud-only accounts cannot use SSPR when Microsoft Entra Connect is synchronizing identities into the tenant.
opzione_b: Accounts with an administrator role are subject to the strong two-gate password reset policy, which requires two authentication methods and prohibits security questions.
opzione_c: Number of days before users are asked to reconfirm their authentication information is set to 0, which blocks administrator resets.
opzione_d: Password writeback is not enabled in Microsoft Entra Connect.
spiegazione: Correct: Administrator accounts are enabled for SSPR by default and are governed by a strong default two-gate password reset policy that cannot be changed. The two-gate policy requires two pieces of authentication data - such as an email address, authenticator app, or phone number - and it prohibits security questions. Helpdesk Administrator appears in the list of roles affected by the two-gate policy, and because a custom domain is configured and Microsoft Entra Connect is synchronizing identities, the two-gate policy applies rather than the one-gate exception. A is wrong: cloud-only accounts are fully supported for SSPR in a hybrid tenant; the presence of Microsoft Entra Connect only affects whether the two-gate policy applies and whether writeback is needed for synchronized users. C is wrong: setting the reconfirmation interval to 0 means users are never asked to confirm their authentication information - it does not block resets, and it is only available when Require users to register when signing in is enabled. D is wrong: the account is cloud-only, so its password is managed in Microsoft Entra ID and writeback is not involved; writeback only matters for federated, pass-through authentication, or password hash synchronized users. Correction: option A was rewritten - it previously claimed the account was not a member of the group selected under Self service password reset enabled, which is incoherent because the scenario sets the scope to All, so no group is selected at all.

domanda: Password writeback is enabled in Microsoft Entra Connect and the option "Write back passwords to your on-premises directory" is selected on the On-premises integration page. Synchronized users can reset their forgotten passwords successfully. However, a user who resets her password and then realizes she mistyped it receives an error when she tries to change it again the same day. Password writeback works normally the next day. What should you configure to resolve the issue?
opzione_a: Grant the Microsoft Entra Connect account the Unexpire Password extended right on the root object of the domain.
opzione_b: Set the Minimum password age group policy setting to 0 in the on-premises domain.
opzione_c: Set Allow users to unlock accounts without resetting their password to Yes on the On-premises integration page.
opzione_d: Set Number of days before users are asked to reconfirm their authentication information to 0.
spiegazione: Correct: On-premises password policies can prevent password resets from being processed. Microsoft Learn states that for password writeback to work most efficiently the Minimum password age group policy must be set to 0, and explicitly notes that if you need to allow users to change or reset passwords more than once per day, you must set Minimum password age to 0. The setting is under Computer Configuration > Policies > Windows Settings > Security Settings > Account Policies in gpmc.msc. A is wrong: the Unexpire Password extended right is a required writeback permission, but a missing one would break writeback consistently, not only for a second reset within the same day - and writeback already works for the first reset. C is wrong: that setting only separates the account-unlock operation from the password-reset operation; it has no effect on how frequently a password can be changed. D is wrong: the reconfirmation interval governs how often users are prompted to confirm their registered authentication information; it does not influence on-premises password age policy.
tags: sspr,password writeback,minimum password age,group policy,troubleshooting,microsoft entra connect

domanda: You are preparing to enable self-service password reset (SSPR) password writeback for a hybrid Microsoft Entra tenant. You must configure the on-premises Active Directory Domain Services permissions for the account that Microsoft Entra Connect uses to synchronize the directory. Which permissions and rights must you grant to that account? Select all that apply. Each correct answer presents part of the solution.
opzione_c: Replicating Directory Changes and Replicating Directory Changes All
opzione_e: Membership in the Enterprise Admins group of the forest root domain
spiegazione: Correct: Microsoft Learn lists the permissions and options that must be set on the account specified in Microsoft Entra Connect for SSPR writeback: Reset password, Change password, Write permissions on lockoutTime, Write permissions on pwdLastSet, and the Extended rights for Unexpire Password on the root object of each domain in that forest. Of the options offered, Reset password, Write pwdLastSet and Write lockoutTime are the three that appear in that list; they are applied to Descendant User objects in Active Directory Users and Computers. (Change password and the Unexpire Password extended right are also required in a real deployment but are not offered as options here.) C is wrong: Replicating Directory Changes and Replicating Directory Changes All are the directory replication permissions used by Microsoft Entra Connect for password hash synchronization; they are not part of the documented writeback permission set. E is wrong: Enterprise Admins membership is never listed as a requirement - granting it would violate least privilege, and the documented approach is to delegate the specific permissions on the domain root instead. If you do not assign the documented permissions, writeback might appear to be configured correctly but users encounter errors when they manage their on-premises passwords from the cloud.

domanda: To satisfy a compliance requirement, you change Guest user access in the external collaboration settings of your Microsoft Entra tenant to "Guest user access is restricted to properties and memberships of their own directory objects (most restrictive)". A B2B collaboration guest user named Ben is affected by the change and holds no directory role. Which actions can Ben still perform by default? Select all that apply. Each correct answer presents part of the solution.
opzione_b: Enumerate the list of all users in the directory
opzione_c: Invite other guest users, if the Guest invite settings allow it
opzione_d: Read the display name and email address of other users in the directory
opzione_e: Manage his own mobile phone number
spiegazione: Correct: The "Restricted guest user permissions" column of the member/guest comparison table on Microsoft Learn lists exactly four Users and contacts capabilities: read their own properties, invite other guests if allowed by Guest invite settings, change their own password, and manage their own mobile phone number. That confirms A, C and E. B is wrong: enumerating the list of all users and contacts is a member user permission only; it is absent from both the default guest and the restricted guest columns. D is wrong: reading the display name, email, sign-in name, photo, user principal name, and user type of other users belongs to the DEFAULT guest permission set ("limited access"), but the most restrictive setting removes it - access to other users is no longer allowed even when searching by user principal name, object ID, or display name. Note that guests can still be added to administrator roles regardless of this setting, which would grant them broader access. Correction: the explanation previously claimed that "guests cannot enumerate the directory at any guest access level", which is not accurate - if Guest user access is set to "Guest users have the same access as members (most inclusive)", guests receive member permissions, which do include enumerating users and groups. The claim is true only for the default and restricted levels.
tags: guest permissions,restricted guest access,default user permissions,b2b collaboration,external collaboration settings

domanda:
You are deploying self-service password reset (SSPR) for Northwind Traders. The deployment must meet the following requirements:
- SSPR must be enabled only for the members of a single Microsoft Entra group named NW-Pilot.
- Users must provide two authentication methods to reset or unlock their password.
- Users must be prompted to register their authentication methods the next time they sign in to a Microsoft Entra integrated application.
- After they register, users must never be prompted to reconfirm their authentication information.
Select the appropriate option for each setting under Entra ID > Password reset.
opzione_a: Self service password reset enabled (Properties page): [None | Selected | All]
opzione_b: Number of methods required to reset (Authentication methods page): [1 | 2 | 3]
opzione_c: Require users to register when signing in (Registration page): [Yes | No]
opzione_d: Number of days before users are asked to reconfirm their authentication information (Registration page): [0 | 180 | 730]
spiegazione: Correct: (1) Self service password reset enabled must be Selected, because SSPR can be scoped to None, Selected, or All, and only Selected scopes SSPR to a single chosen Microsoft Entra group - None would disable SSPR and All would enable every user in the tenant. (2) Number of methods required to reset must be 2; Microsoft Learn states this value can be set to either one or two, so 3 is not a valid choice and 1 would not meet the requirement. (3) Require users to register when signing in must be Yes, which prompts users to complete SSPR registration when they use modern authentication or a web browser to sign in to applications that use Microsoft Entra ID; No means users are never prompted during sign-in and must register manually at https://aka.ms/ssprsetup. (4) The reconfirmation interval accepts values from 0 to 730 days, and setting the value to 0 means users are never asked to confirm their authentication information - 180 and 730 would both prompt users to reconfirm. Note that the reconfirmation setting is only available when Require users to register when signing in is enabled. Correction: the stem and options were clarified to name the page that hosts each setting - the four settings are not all on the Properties page; scope is on Properties, the method count is on Authentication methods, and both registration settings are on Registration.
tags: sspr,registration,number of methods required,reconfirm authentication information,microsoft entra id

domanda:
Adventure Works collaborates with two partner organizations that use the domains fabrikam.com and litware.com. You must configure the external collaboration settings of the Microsoft Entra tenant to meet the following requirements:
- Guest users must be able to see only their own profile information. They must not be able to see other users, groups, or group memberships.
- Only users who hold the User Administrator or Guest Inviter role may send B2B collaboration invitations.
- Invitations may be sent only to fabrikam.com and litware.com. Invitations to every other domain must fail.
Select the appropriate option for each setting.
opzione_a: Guest user access: [Guest users have the same access as members (most inclusive) | Guest users have limited access to properties and memberships of directory objects | Guest user access is restricted to properties and memberships of their own directory objects (most restrictive)]
opzione_b: Guest invite settings: [Anyone in the organization can invite guest users including guests and non-admins (most inclusive) | Member users and users assigned to specific admin roles can invite guest users including guests with member permissions | Only users assigned to specific admin roles can invite guest users | No one in the organization can invite guest users including admins (most restrictive)]
opzione_c: Collaboration restrictions: [Allow invitations to be sent to any domain (most inclusive) | Deny invitations to the specified domains | Allow invitations only to the specified domains (most restrictive)]
risposta_corretta: Guest user access is restricted to properties and memberships of their own directory objects (most restrictive),Only users assigned to specific admin roles can invite guest users,Allow invitations only to the specified domains (most restrictive)
spiegazione: Correct: (1) "Guest user access is restricted to properties and memberships of their own directory objects (most restrictive)" is the only level where guests can access only their own profiles and are not allowed to see other users' profiles, groups, or group memberships. "Same access as members" gives guests member-equivalent directory access, and the default "limited access" still lets guests see the membership of all non-hidden groups and read basic properties of other users. (2) "Only users assigned to specific admin roles can invite guest users" is documented as allowing only those users with the User Administrator or Guest Inviter role to invite guests. The "Anyone in the organization" option would let guests and non-admins invite; "Member users and users assigned to specific admin roles" would still let all member users invite; "No one in the organization" would block everyone including admins, so no invitations could be sent at all. (3) "Allow invitations only to the specified domains (most restrictive)" creates an allow list, so only the listed target domains can receive invitations and invitations to every other domain fail with a blocked-domain message. "Allow invitations to be sent to any domain" is the default and imposes no restriction; "Deny invitations to the specified domains" is a block list, which would require listing every domain in the world except the two partners. Remember you can create either an allow list or a block list, but not both, and only one policy per organization is supported. Note this list is checked at invitation time and does not apply to guests who already redeemed an invitation.
tags: external collaboration settings,guest user access,guest invite settings,collaboration restrictions,allow list,b2b

domanda:
The Microsoft Entra tenant for Contoso, Ltd. has the custom domain contoso.com verified, and Microsoft Entra Connect synchronizes identities from an on-premises Active Directory Domain Services forest. On the Password reset blade, Self service password reset enabled is set to Selected and scoped to a group named Sales. Number of methods required to reset is set to 2. The members of Sales previously registered only a mobile phone, because the policy formerly required a single method. Evaluate whether each of the following statements is true.
1. A member of Sales who has registered only a mobile phone can still reset a forgotten password by using SSPR.
2. A cloud-only user who is assigned the User Administrator role can register security questions and use them as one of the two methods required to reset the password.
3. To prevent administrator accounts from using SSPR, you must set the AllowedToUseSspr property on the tenant authorization policy to false.
opzione_a: A member of Sales who has registered only a mobile phone can still reset a forgotten password by using SSPR.
opzione_b: A cloud-only user who is assigned the User Administrator role can register security questions and use them as one of the two methods required to reset the password.
opzione_c: To prevent administrator accounts from using SSPR, you must set the AllowedToUseSspr property on the tenant authorization policy to false.
spiegazione: Statement 1 - No: The "Change authentication methods" table on Microsoft Learn documents the outcome of changing the number of required methods: 1 method registered with 2 methods required gives the result "Unable to reset or unlock". Users who do not register the minimum number of required methods see an error page and must request that an administrator reset their password. Statement 2 - No: User Administrator is one of the administrator roles listed as being affected by the strong default two-gate password reset policy, and because the tenant has a custom domain configured and Microsoft Entra Connect synchronizing identities, the two-gate policy applies rather than the one-gate exception. The two-gate policy requires two pieces of authentication data such as an email address, authenticator app, or phone number, and it explicitly prohibits security questions. Statement 3 - Yes: You can disable the use of SSPR for administrator accounts by setting the value of the AllowedToUseSspr property on the tenant authorization policy to false, for example with Update-MgPolicyAuthorizationPolicy -AllowedToUseSspr:$false, or by PATCHing allowedToUseSSPR on the authorizationPolicy in Microsoft Graph. Administrators are enabled for SSPR by default and the administrator two-gate policy itself cannot be edited, so this tenant-level property is the supported way to turn it off. Policy changes can take up to 60 minutes to take effect.
tags: sspr,two-gate policy,allowedtousesspr,authorization policy,number of methods required,administrator reset policy

domanda:
In the external collaboration settings of the Microsoft Entra tenant for Woodgrove Bank, Collaboration restrictions is currently set to "Deny invitations to the specified domains" and fabrikam.com is listed as a target domain. Several guest users from other domains have already redeemed their invitations. Evaluate whether each of the following statements is true.
1. While the deny list is in place, you can also configure an allow list that contains contoso.com so that invitations to contoso.com are explicitly permitted.
2. If you switch the setting to "Allow invitations only to the specified domains (most restrictive)", the existing deny list configuration is discarded.
3. The deny list also prevents users from sharing individual SharePoint Online and OneDrive files with users in fabrikam.com.
opzione_a: While the deny list is in place, you can also configure an allow list that contains contoso.com so that invitations to contoso.com are explicitly permitted.
opzione_b: If you switch the setting to "Allow invitations only to the specified domains (most restrictive)", the existing deny list configuration is discarded.
opzione_c: The deny list also prevents users from sharing individual SharePoint Online and OneDrive files with users in fabrikam.com.
spiegazione: Statement 1 - No: Microsoft Learn is explicit that you can create either an allow list or a block list, but you can't set up both types of lists. By default, whatever domains are not in the allow list are on the block list, and vice versa. Only one policy per organization is supported; you can update the policy to include more domains, or delete the policy to create a new one. Statement 2 - Yes: The "Switch from allow list to block list and vice versa" section states that switching from one policy to another discards the existing policy configuration, which is why the documentation advises backing up the details of your configuration before you perform the switch. Statement 3 - No: This list works independently from the OneDrive and SharePoint Online allow/block lists. To restrict individual file sharing in SharePoint Online you must set up a separate allow or block list for OneDrive and SharePoint Online. Also note that the list does not apply to external users who have already redeemed their invitation - it is enforced only from the time it is set up, although a pending invitation whose domain becomes blocked will fail at redemption.
tags: allow list,block list,collaboration restrictions,b2b invitations,external collaboration settings

domanda: Case study: Litware, Inc. has a Microsoft Entra tenant named litware.onmicrosoft.com with the verified custom domain litware.com. A Microsoft Entra Connect server synchronizes the on-premises Active Directory Domain Services forest to the tenant by using password hash synchronization. All 2,000 users are assigned Microsoft Entra ID P1 licenses. On the Password reset blade, Self service password reset enabled is set to All and Number of methods required to reset is set to 2. All users have registered a mobile phone and an authentication email. On the Microsoft Entra Connect server, the Password writeback check box is selected on the Optional features page, and the synchronization account has been granted Reset password, Change password, Write lockoutTime, Write pwdLastSet, and the Unexpire Password extended right. Cloud-only users can reset their passwords at https://aka.ms/sspr without any problem. Every synchronized user who attempts a reset is instead told to contact an administrator to reset the password. You need to resolve the issue for the synchronized users. What should you do?
opzione_a: In the Microsoft Entra admin center, browse to Entra ID > Password reset > On-premises integration and select "Write back passwords to your on-premises directory".
opzione_b: In the Microsoft Entra admin center, browse to Entra ID > Password reset > Properties and set Number of methods required to reset to 1.
opzione_c: Reconfigure Microsoft Entra Connect to use pass-through authentication instead of password hash synchronization.
opzione_d: In the Microsoft Entra admin center, browse to Entra ID > Password reset > On-premises integration and set "Allow users to unlock accounts without resetting their password" to Yes.
spiegazione: Correct: Enabling password writeback is a two-part configuration. Selecting Password writeback on the Optional features page of Microsoft Entra Connect is only the first half; you must also enable writeback for SSPR in the Microsoft Entra admin center under Entra ID > Password reset > On-premises integration by checking "Write back passwords to your on-premises directory" (as at least a Hybrid Identity Administrator). Microsoft Learn states that when this option is set to No, writeback is disabled and federated, pass-through authentication, or password hash synchronized users aren't able to reset their passwords. This matches the symptom exactly: during the SSPR checks, Microsoft Entra ID determines that the user's password is managed on-premises, and if SSPR writeback isn't deployed the user is asked to contact their administrator - while cloud-only users are unaffected. B is wrong: all users have registered two methods, so the method count check is already satisfied; lowering it to 1 would weaken security and would not change the on-premises password management check (and the setting lives on the Authentication methods page, not Properties). C is wrong: pass-through authentication also leaves the password managed on-premises, so the same writeback check applies - switching sign-in methods does not enable writeback. D is wrong: "Allow users to unlock accounts without resetting their password" only separates the account-unlock operation from the password-reset operation for users whose writeback is already working; it does not enable writeback.
tags: sspr,password writeback,on-premises integration,microsoft entra connect,password hash synchronization,troubleshooting
